recognize_zh: 視野中央的淋巴球細胞質量中等、淡藍色，內含許多細小的嗜天青紫紅色顆粒，核圓略偏位、染色質成塊，是典型大顆粒淋巴球（LGL）的樣子。
features: Single lymphocyte slightly larger than a small lymphocyte, with moderate pale blue cytoplasm
Numerous fine azurophilic granules distributed throughout the cytoplasm
Round, slightly eccentric nucleus with coarsely clumped mature chromatin and no nucleolus
Background red cells with mild ovalocytosis; scattered normal platelets
No other leukocytes in the field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a single large granular lymphocyte with moderate amounts of pale cytoplasm containing numerous fine azurophilic granules and a round, slightly eccentric nucleus with mature clumped chromatin. Background red cells show mild ovalocytosis, and platelets appear adequate in this field. The cell is a morphologically normal large granular lymphocyte (cytotoxic T or NK cell); if LGLs are persistently increased with cytopenias, flow cytometry and T-cell receptor clonality studies are indicated to evaluate for LGL leukemia.

ddx.dx: T-LGL leukemia / chronic lymphoproliferative disorder of NK cells
ddx.vs: Cannot be separated by single-cell morphology; requires a sustained LGL lymphocytosis with an immunophenotypically abnormal, clonal population.
Myeloid precursors are larger with more abundant cytoplasm, coarser primary granules or pink secondary granules, and finer chromatin, sometimes with a Golgi zone.
Basophils have large, dark purple-black granules that obscure the nucleus rather than fine sparse azurophilic granules.
Reactive lymphocytes have more abundant, basophilic cytoplasm that scallops around red cells and generally lack discrete azurophilic granules.
